cards.title: One-Species Scaling Coefficients for Human CL
cards.claim: Data-driven one-species methods for predicting human clearance (CL) were derived as: CL(human)/kg = 0.152 x CL(rat)/kg, CL(human)/kg = 0.410 x CL(dog)/kg, and CL(human)/kg = 0.407 x CL(monkey)/kg. The monkey method coefficient (0.407) was similar to the monkey LBF method (0.467), while rat (0.152) and dog (0.410) coefficients differed significantly from their respective LBF methods (0.247 and 0.700).
conditions: Applicable for prospective human CL prediction when only one animal species data is available.
Coefficients are specific to the dataset (n=102) and method derivation.
Not a universal constant; applicability depends on compound class and similarity to training set.
required_inputs: Animal CL data (rat, dog, or monkey) normalized to body weight (CL/kg).
Human body weight (implied by /kg normalization in formula).
limitations: Abstract-only source; full methodology for coefficient derivation not visible.
Coefficients are fixed values from this specific study; not validated for all drug classes.
Does not account for protein binding or specific metabolic pathways beyond the aggregate CL data.
cards.downstream_use: Use these specific linear scaling factors as candidate methods for human CL prediction in translation modules, comparing against standard allometric scaling.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
